subject: grayWolf
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: gray wolf standing alert.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
Looking at the renders, the mane tufts read as big dark flat shards sticking out like spiky armor rather than fur—I need to shrink them and angle them back along the body, and the cream cheek ruff blades are crowding the face too much.

The collar strap also looks like a floating brown arc detached from the neck instead of sitting flush against it. The legs are too long and thin, making the body look skinny and stiff, and the jaw reads as a separate tube hanging below the head with a visible gap, giving it an awkward gaping-mouth look that I need to close up by adjusting the jaw's position relative to the head loft.

I'm also noticing some stray cream-colored tuft elements sitting oddly on top of the head that need to be removed, and the head seems too small relative to the broad shoulders and deep chest, though it may be fine to leave as is given the complexity of repositioning everything. The mane tufts are the main remaining issue to address next.

I'm reconsidering the plate orientation — angling the width direction so the shards read as thin edge-on from the side but wider from behind, aiming for a layered fur-card look rather than giant flat shards. I'll shrink and reduce the lateral flank tufts that are currently reading as oversized grey-dark shards in three-quarter view, keeping just a smaller, sparser set.

Adjusting ruff tuft size and placement...

Now I'm questioning whether the collar band is floating weird in the close-up — it arcs off the neck like a hoop near the cheek, so I'm considering lifting it slightly and checking if the loop plane is tilted relative to the neck. Rather than fighting this geometry, maybe it's safer to rebuild the collar as a separate torus-ring part instead.

Placing a torus at the neck's midpoint, oriented along the tangent with its axis set to Z, sized to roughly match the neck's circumference there and skinned to the right bone. I'm keeping the bead ring and fang pendant positioning as before, just adjusting the collar approach.

Switching the collar beads to use a bone ring helper with 14 beads at that same neck radius. Checking that the ruff tufts near the neck don't overlap badly with the collar — since the tufts point backward toward the shoulders and the collar sits slightly higher, they shouldn't conflict visually.

The dark tuft cards on the back still read fine as spiky shards, so I'll leave those. Legs, paws, tail, and the base-to-wolf size ratio all look acceptable as is — I might just nudge the base position slightly, but otherwise keep the current proportions.

Now I need to reposition the banner pole so it doesn't collide with the snout in three-quarter view; checking the distance from center against the decagon base radius, I'll move it to roughly x=-0.95, z=0.7, which keeps it clear of the wolf's nose and head while staying inside the base.

With that settled, I'm turning to the mane tufts, shrinking the loop that generates each tuft and adjusting their directions and lengths for the top and flank sections so they sit more naturally against the head.

Settling on the direction vector for the plate orientation, then moving to locate and remove the ear tuft loop code.

I'm also planning edits to the cheek ruff angle array and the jaw sweep's catmull points, adjusting the jaw curve to sit slightly higher.

I need to check that the jaw's radius tapering keeps it overlapping cleanly with the head's bottom edge rather than leaving a gap, and nudge the lower fang position upward slightly to about 1.068 so it reads as pointing up correctly.

Now I'm rewriting the collar section, replacing the earlier block with sweep geometry anchored to the neck joint, then looping through to place alternating beads of ice, bone, and dark leather colors along the collar path.

Keeping the position reference off neck.at(0.55) and now adjusting the banner's BX and BZ constants.
